story_type: magnetically levitated rocket sled sets a speed record
hook: This rocket sled floats on magnets. Watch it set a world record.
narration: This rocket sled floats on magnets, and it is about to set a world record.
On March fourth, twenty sixteen, the eight forty sixth Test Squadron fired it down a twenty one hundred foot track at Holloman Air Force Base, New Mexico.
Very cold liquid helium chills superconducting magnets, and those magnets lift the sled off the rail.
Two days earlier, it had already broken the record at five hundred thirteen miles per hour.
outcome: The sled hit six hundred thirty three miles per hour, a world record for a magnetic levitation sled.

location_card.place: Holloman Air Force Base, New Mexico

title: Rocket sled on magnets hits 633 mph
description:
The 846th Test Squadron's magnetically levitated rocket sled reaches 633 miles per hour on the 2,100-foot MagLev track at Holloman Air Force Base, New Mexico, on March 4, 2016.

Footage: U.S. Air Force video by Senior Airman BreeAnn Sachs, 49th Wing Public Affairs, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/459596/maglev-world-record
